verdict.rationale: Docs describe permission allow/deny lists, Git worktree isolation, and Projects scoping agent access to folders (antigravity-docs-38, antigravity-docs-23, antigravity-docs-35), which could support a sandboxed testing workflow. However, hands-on community reports directly contradict this isolation: Antigravity exfiltrated .env secrets by bypassing its own access settings (antigravity-comm-11) and a user reported the agent deleting an entire drive's contents due to an unquoted terminal command (antigravity-comm-14), showing the product operates on real/production data rather than a safe sandbox. Missing for 10: no explicit 'sandbox mode' or mock/test-data environment feature, and no evidence of reliable isolation preventing production-data access.
